title: Cursor vs Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot — Which AI Coding Tool Actually Wins? (2026)
summary: Desk-research comparison of Cursor, Claude Code and Copilot using benchmarks, surveys and pricing, with caveats on contamination.

assertions.quote: SWE-Bench Verified has a contamination problem

verdicts.note: Contamination and memorization in SWE-bench Verified are documented, and scores drop substantially on SWE-bench Pro and fresh benchmarks.

assertions.quote: Claude's Opus models have posted the highest scores of the three

verdicts.note: Claude models have often topped SWE-bench and similar leaderboards, but GPT-5.x/Codex and Gemini models trade the lead release to release; also, Cursor and Copilot can run Claude models.

assertions.quote: Copilot wins on raw speed for inline completions

verdicts.note: Copilot's broad IDE support is true, but by 2026 it has agent mode and multi-file edits; 'smaller context' framing is dated.

assertions.quote: Cursor wins on day-to-day speed and the all-in-one IDE experience

verdicts.note: Cursor's indexing and model choice are accurate; 'most integrated' is a taste judgment and competitors have closed gaps.

assertions.quote: Claude code wins on raw benchmark performance and autonomous, complex tasks

verdicts.note: Claude Code is widely regarded as strong on autonomous multi-step tasks, but 'best' varies by task and model release; Codex and others compete.

assertions.quote: most experienced developers aren't picking just one

verdicts.note: Developer surveys (e.g. Stack Overflow 2025) show many use multiple AI tools concurrently.
By 2026 the major tools all offer agents, CLIs, cloud runs and review; differences are workflow and pricing more than capability.

assertions.quote: Copilot wins on price and editor flexibility

verdicts.note: Copilot Pro's $10 tier is the cheapest headline price and GitHub integration is real; 'best fit' depends on team needs.
